system.summary: Letter substitution with a few homophones and several signs that stand for two to four letters as transcribed (look-alike shapes not yet split), word signs (je, le, que, la, pour) and name codes (la Rochelle, Monsieur du Mayne), and nulls including a divider stroke. Tomokiyo's 'St. Luc's Cipher' table, corrected by Brackx.
system.doubled_letters: Separate signs for rr, ll, ss and mm.
system.sibling_key: Same table as St. Luc's f. 245r-v (with contemporary margin decipherments). Not the cipher of f. 43 (saintluc1586, George Lasry's key), which is another table.
system.notes: Labels are Brackx's (brackx2026/label_legend.md). Multi-valued labels (z = u/v/h/m, 9 and 9q = n/m/g, S = m/s/g/mm, f = c/s, p = i/r, 6 = s/y, y = n/d, d = l/c/p, t/tb = p/t/v/r, pi = f/s) carry 40.5% of the letters on f. 260r and 34.5% on f. 260v; they are most likely look-alike shapes merged in transcription, not designed polyphony, but that is not yet shown on the image.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana henryiii page, 'St. Luc's Cipher': the key table and the opening line of f. 260 ('arriva hier en Olleron ... sans retourner a'); f. 260 otherwise called undeciphered. No other reading found (Brackx, web search; this repository).

conditions.human_role: Michael Brackx, working with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), transcribed f. 245r-v and f. 260r-v sign by sign, corrected Tomokiyo's table on the f. 245 margin decipherments, decoded f. 260 with a beam search under a French model and built a reading line by line with English (issue #90). In this repository: measurement against the read bar, the look-alike grading, the target record and write-up; two blind shape plates answered by Brice Dudout (25 Nov 2026), built and scored with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5).
tools: Brackx's align.py, cover.py and crib scorer (not in the repository)

solution.what: Tomokiyo's 'St. Luc's Cipher' table (cryptiana henryiii) encoded as labels with values; nulls and the word signs kept (Brackx, #90).
f. 245r-v (cipher passages, 423 signs) and f. 260r-v (26 and 29 lines, 2,428 tokens) transcribed sign by sign from deskewed full-size line crops (Brackx with Claude Code, #90).

The margin decipherments of f. 245v (crib 1) and f. 245r (crib 2) aligned with their cipher: key corrections Δo = Monsieur du Mayne, ʞ = pour, ⊔ = la Rochelle, new signs ss and la, Ↄ = rr, crossed ʒ = h, plain 3 = m, ♀/♁ = n/p, x; letter agreement 89.3% (f. 245v) and 83.2% (f. 245r) under the corrected Essais model, shuffled-key controls 11-31%.

f. 260r-v decoded by beam search over each label's allowed values under a French character 5-gram; 741 single-value key candidates tried; corpus-word coverage 79.2% / 80.7% (controls 27-46% / 31-49%). A decoder bug that skipped lines beginning with the label # was fixed (r. 8, v. 19 restored).

Brackx's reading of f. 260r-v in the writer's spelling with every unread run sized and an English translation (#90, reply of 23 Oct 2026): Oléron, the shallops and galliots, the stone-laden ships against the palisade, the unpaid garrison, the Rochelais passports and the salt of the grand parti. 22 letters read with another value of the same label than the decoder chose.

Read bar applied (v10_relabel.measure): f. 260r 0.761 and f. 260v 0.851 of words read as sense. Letters on multi-valued labels are 40.5% / 34.5% of the text, over the 3% look-alike limit, so both pages are graded decoded, not read whatever their share; the readings are kept as partial readings with English.

Method restored: key obtained by Tomokiyo's published St. Luc table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments (read with known key); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

Brackx (issue #95) re-located every token of the four largest multi-valued labels on the full-size images by template matching and cut contact sheets by decoded value: ϙ 9 (126 n, 12 m, 12 g), ʒ z (117 u, 15 m, 5 h), б 6 (161 s, 32 y), ρ p (125 i, 17 r). No label splits by shape; only part of each minority value located cleanly. Look-alike share unchanged at 40.5% / 34.5%.

Brackx (issue #99) split-tested the remaining six multi-valued labels on the f. 260 images: S splits (§§ = mm, long s = s; r. 23 dosame -> dommage) and d splits (hooked arch = l, ∂ = c); f, t/tb, pi, y do not. Look-alike share 40.5% -> 39.4% (f. 260r), 34.5% -> 33.8% (f. 260v); both pages stay decoded, not read.

Blind shape plate A (blind_check/, Brice Dudout, 13 boxed signs, 3 hidden controls passed): at places where the reading needs a value the label lacks, the reviewer chose among distinct signs of the table. ʒ at v. 20 r42, r46, v. 23 r32, v. 24 r47 matched z (u) and r. 1 r7 matched zc (h): leuee, du, guerre, uos and hier read with the plate. At the three 9-read-q places and the two P-read-ff places he saw a shape not offered (a q with two bars; a stem with a triangular flag). f. 260r 0.761 -> 0.764, f. 260v 0.851 -> 0.866 (v10).

Blind shape plate B (blind_check/, 8 boxed signs, 3 hidden controls passed), with every plausible shape of the table plus the two shapes described on plate A: 3 of 3 9-read-q targets chose the two-barred ϙ (one answer with a remark that one distractor showed two different signs, the chosen value being single, kept) and 2 of 2 P-read-ff targets chose the flagged stem. The two shapes are stable; proposed labels Q2B = q and FF = ff, values by sense only, so the words stay doubtful. v. 3 [?quinse] and v. 9 [?effect] added as doubtful words. Read shares unchanged (0.764 / 0.866); both pages stay decoded, not read.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's published table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments, decodes f. 260r-v into French that largely builds sentences (0.761 / 0.851 of words), but 40.5% / 34.5% of the letters fall on labels with several values chosen by a language model, so the text is decoded, not read. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by Tomokiyo's published St. Luc table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments; class stays not read, as the text does not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 25 Nov 2026 (after the blind shape plates): texts/reading_f260r.md 0.764 and reading_f260v.md 0.866 of words read as sense (v10; 0.761 / 0.851 on 24 Oct), but both decoded, not read under the look-alike limit, so nothing counts as read.

gaps.item: multi-valued labels on f. 260r-v (z, 9/9q, S, f, p, 6, y, d, t/tb, pi): 40.5% of the letters on f. 260r, 34.5% on f. 260v
gaps.detail: all ten multi-valued labels split-tested by shape on the full-size images (Brackx, issues #95 and #99): S (mm / s) and d (l / c) split, the other eight do not; look-alike share now 39.4% / 33.8%. Only a contemporary decipherment of f. 260 or another letter in this key would settle the remaining choices

gaps.item: open runs: r. 1-2 (places after en son), r. 5-11, r. 13-14, r. 17, r. 19-24; v. 3 (the day in April), v. 4, v. 8-9, v. 12-18, v. 23, v. 27
gaps.detail: to be retried after the label split; one [?] per unread word or group in texts/reading_f260r.md, reading_f260v.md

gaps.item: two sign shapes not in the label legend, given values by sense only: a ϙ with two bars across the stem (proposed `Q2B` = q, 4 tokens: r. 23 r3, v. 13 r14, v. 26 r18, v. 3 r20; all now labelled 9 or t2) and a stem with a triangular flag (proposed `FF` = ff, 4 tokens: v. 25 r2, v. 27 r2, v. 9 r2, v. 9 r35; labelled P or v)
gaps.detail: both shapes confirmed on the blind plates of 25 Nov 2026 (blind_check/): 3 of 3 targets answered Q2B, 2 of 2 answered FF, controls 6 of 6. The values q and ff come from the sense of the words only (consequence, quand, ce qu'il, quinse; affaires, affaire, effect, affin): Tomokiyo's table has neither shape and f. 245 does not use them, so these words stay doubtful. A sign at v. 9 r14 (labelled 9, ϙ with a bar) may be a fifth Q2B; not on a plate

outcome.notes: New item, not in the catalogue or on DECODE as far as found. Contributed by Michael Brackx, issue #90. Separate from saintluc1586 (f. 43, another table, George Lasry's key).

texts.label: f. 260r
texts.summary: St. Luc to Henri III from Brouage, June 1586: a Rochelais commander has come to Oléron and watched his galliots attack the Brouage shallops; the Rochelais try to block the harbour with ships loaded with stone, one of six score tons, and the garrison has taken one of them.
texts.note: 25 Nov 2026: 76.4% of the words of texts/reading_f260r.md read as sense (v10; 76.1% before the blind shape plate of 25 Nov, dudout/), and 39.4% of the letters fall on multi-valued labels (3% look-alike limit): decoded, not read. Brackx's reading is kept as a partial reading.

texts.label: f. 260v
texts.summary: The garrison is unpaid and losing hope, with no word of the King's commands since April; La Rochelle means to keep the sea and sell passports to its captains; St. Luc protests that the council has let the tax-farmers of the grand parti buy salt at La Rochelle and asks that French merchants be forbidden to take salt there on pain of confiscation.
texts.note: 25 Nov 2026: 86.6% of the words of texts/reading_f260v.md read as sense (v10; 85.1% before the blind shape plate of 25 Nov, dudout/), and 33.8% of the letters fall on multi-valued labels (3% look-alike limit): decoded, not read. Brackx's reading is kept as a partial reading.
